reply_text:
㊥ (gist) I take "the task" to mean resuming the mfuton row loop under the best-of preamble. I think that's half right. The lane work is procedural enough for any agent to do. The integration owner's role is not, and that's where the 10-06 failures happened.

🈖 (why the lanes can go to any agent) The preamble now turns a lane into a fixed procedure:
1. Read the raise site and Lean's source.
2. Write the two step lists side by side.
3. Fix at the first point where they diverge.
4. Predict the result, run cold once, and report prediction against result.

It also limits how far a weak run can go wrong: a wrong prediction stops the lane, and the cold comparator decides, not the agent's own word. The WHY note supports this: "The agents did what the packets asked." They also found the real causes three times when the owner's diagnosis was wrong.

🚫 (why the owner's role can't go to just any agent) Every failure in the WHY note came from the owner. It accepted a "clean" prediction without evidence, put its own wrong diagnoses into packets, and twice accepted tests that swapped in a stand-in for the step under test. The best-of preamble doesn't remove that judgment. It gives the owner more of it to exercise:
- deciding whether a reading really shows the line runs
- deciding whether a stopped lane's explanation holds up
- choosing what the next packet asks

My memory notes also say Zai seats that own work tend to stall, so that's the one role I wouldn't hand to a cheap seat. Rule 6 makes this matter more: every wrong prediction waits for the owner, so a slow or weak owner holds up the whole loop.

㊭ (how to find out cheaply) Give one discovery packet under the draft preamble to a Zai seat and the same packet to a Codex seat, and score both reports against rules 1–3:
- facts with file:line
- both step lists
- evidence that the line actually runs

A discovery packet can't break anything, and one round shows whether a cheap seat follows the procedure or only sounds like it does. zai-1's reconstruction job is a smaller test of the same thing, and I'll know how it went when it reports back.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(how they differ) Preamble 7 is a rewrite of 6 based on what went wrong on 10-06, and it's stronger on method. Its additions:
- facts, not confirmations
- Lean's steps listed beside the port's calls
- show the line runs
- no fix before its discovery returns
- the capture-tool caveat

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-11
previous_reply_acts.text:
(two places I chose, which you may want to overrule)
1. **Unit tests.** Preamble 6 contradicts itself here. Its "red means the defect" and real-path rules demand failing-first unit tests. Its own later "TEST RULE REVISED" says not to build unit tests for elaboration changes, because the real-path ones can't be built and stubbed ones passed while production didn't change. I took 7's resolution: the cold comparator is the test, and unit tests are only for tools.
2. **A wrong prediction.** Preamble 6 says go back to reading. Preamble 7 says the lane stops until the integration owner replies. I took 7's stricter version, because it came from the 10-06 failures, and added that reading can continue. The cost is orchestrator latency on every miss.
